text: dsh-knowledge-canvas 是面向 DSH Web 的树状知识库插件，在右侧栏提供可编辑画布，并用主机工具读写工作区内的知识库文件。它支持按会话启用知识库、以大纲或全文注入、为节点设置触发条件、编辑父子节点与关联、查看模型改动标记，并提供会话日记与附件阅读。适合希望跨会话保存项目约定和经验、同时能人工检查和整理笔记的 DSH 用户。无需 API Key 或外部账号；数据保存在工作区。

dsh-knowledge-canvas adds a knowledge canvas to DSH Web, where users edit tree-shaped notes and the model reads or updates them. Select bases per session and inject outlines or full text; nodes support trigger lines, links and review markers. No API key is needed; files stay in the workspace.
想让 DSH 在新会话里也记得项目约定和踩坑经验。
有没有办法把长期笔记整理成树状结构，自己在侧栏维护？
我希望 AI 只在相关任务时读某条知识，而不是每次塞进整篇笔记。
想在 DSH 里把知识库按会话打开或关闭。
怎么给知识节点加上适用时机，让模型知道什么时候想起它？
让模型写入知识后，我想在画布上看到哪些内容需要复核。
我想把有关联的知识条目连起来，并写明为什么相关。
有没有能把每段对话的日记分开保存，还能从侧栏回复的功能？
How can I keep project notes available to DSH across sessions and edit them as a tree?
I want the model to retrieve a note only when its trigger condition applies.
插件在 DSH Web 右侧栏显示知识画布，可创建和编辑节点、调整层级与布局，并浏览关联线。
用户可按会话启用知识库，并选择注入大纲或全文；节点还能覆盖知识库的默认注入方式。
模型通过知识工具创建知识库、读取和改写节点、添加或更新关联，也可软删除节点或知识库。
知识写入会为节点留下改动标记；界面展示变更，用户可检查并恢复未审核或单个节点的改动。
用户可按会话开启独立日记，在侧栏按条目浏览并回复；插件把回复保存为记录，再提交到当前会话。
dsh-knowledge-canvas 将知识库、选择状态和画布布局写入当前工作区的 .dsh-knowledge/ 文件；安装无需 API Key 或外部账号。
dsh-knowledge-canvas 提供工具 knowledge_create_base
dsh-knowledge-canvas 提供工具 knowledge_write_node
dsh-knowledge-canvas 提供工具 knowledge_remove_base

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · dsh-knowledge-canvas：**English** · [简体中文](README.zh.md)

A knowledge base for DeepSeek Harness that the model retrieves from **by judgement, not by similarity** — and that you edit on a canvas in the sidebar.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Features：- Edit knowledge on a canvas: parent/child relationships, associations, four layouts, and resizable nodes.
- Collapse branches and reveal the path to search results. Long notes scroll; title-only nodes offer a reading preview.
- Choose full-text or on-demand injection per base, with individual node overrides.
- Review model edits and inspect which nodes were read, written or removed.
- Read session-scoped diaries as a notebook and reply from the sidebar.
- Attach images and files; choose on-demand or required attachment reading per workspace.
dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Features：[Usage manual](MANUAL.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/NeoHotaru/dsh-knowledge-canvas/releases)

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · The problem：**You explain something, and the next conversation still does not know it — or worse, it thinks it does, and the note is stale.**

This is not a context-window problem. Measured in one workspace:

```
$ node report-kb-use.mjs
50 tool call(s) in the log, 1 session(s)
  写 13 次（ops / …）
  读 1 次（read-animation）

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · The problem：**13 writes, 1 read** — and that read was from a different base. Knowledge was *recorded* and never *used*. Recording is free: the model does it in passing. Using is the hard part: you have to know the entry exists, and which one still holds.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · What makes this different：Every node ends with a line beginning 「什么时候该想起它：」 — "when should this come to mind". That line is what the outline shows, so the model matches a situation rather than an embedding. When it picks wrong, you see the wrong node on the canvas and fix the sentence that misled it.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · On the panel：| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| Top row | search, read counters, refresh |
| One row per base | title, read progress, one switch (does this conversation read it), `⋯` menu (rename, delete, colour, export) |
| Canvas toolbar | zoom, fit, **width** (the whole base's default width, not one node), shape, colour, layout |
| 「定位到…」 at the bottom | type an id to jump to that node |

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · On the panel：| Gesture | Result |
| --- | --- |
| click a node | opens the editor; click again to close |
| Enter / Space (focused) | same, from the keyboard |
| Shift+Enter | start a link; Enter on the target finishes it |
| drag a node | moves it; the drop is written to `layout.json` |
| hold ~0.26 s then drag | draws a **link** (orange), not a re-parent |
| **Alt + drag a node** | makes the target its parent (grey line) |
| right-click a node | fold/expand, injection policy, new child, change history |
| title arrow on a branch | collapse or expand its descendants |
| right-click empty canvas | menu: new top-level node |
| drag a node out to the input box | hands that node to the conversation |
| the three handles | width, height, both |

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · On the panel：Node size means three things in order: this node → the base's default → the canvas zoom. The toolbar's 「宽度」 is the second one.

Four layouts: layers, radial, staircase, compact. Switching recomputes default placement; manual positions stay under your control.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · On the panel：Collapse a branch using its title arrow or context menu. Nested folds are remembered; search, locate and unread navigation reveal the target's ancestor path. The toolbar can expand everything or arrange visible nodes. Folding affects the canvas only, not model access or injection.

Long note bodies scroll independently and offer an Edit action. At title-only zoom levels, hovering or focusing a node opens a reading preview.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Install：```bash
pnpm add dsh-knowledge-canvas@latest
```

Run the command in the intended DSH profile directory. For manual installation, also add `dsh-knowledge-canvas` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in that profile's package.json, preserving existing entries. A dependency alone does not apply the bundle patch. The DSH Add Plugin UI is the recommended installation path.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Install：Source links also use the package name `dsh-knowledge-canvas`. Internal legacy module ids and data paths remain unchanged for compatibility.

Restart DSH once after installing; the 「知识库」 panel appears in the sidebar. Panel-side changes need only a page reload; host-side changes (`index.js`, `lib/*`) need a restart — that distinction decides what you do after editing.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Install：The first time you open a workspace, a base called 「怎么用这个知识库」 is seeded with everything the panel can do. It upgrades with each release, and nodes you edited are never overwritten.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Model tools：| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `knowledge_read` | read a base or a node; without `base`, list the bases |
| `knowledge_create_base` | create a base with a root node. **Usable immediately** — no `knowledge_select` needed |
| `knowledge_write_node` | write or edit a node. The return carries the id it just created, ready to use as `parent` |
| `knowledge_link` | connect two nodes, and say in one line why they are related |
| `knowledge_remove_node` | mark a node removed (recoverable, not deleted) |
| `knowledge_unlink` | remove an association; the nodes stay, the dashed line goes |
| `knowledge_select` | switch a base on or off for this conversation |
| `knowledge_remove_base` | mark a base removed (recoverable; the file is not deleted) |
| `knowledge_show_images` | Hands a node's pictures to the model as images |

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Settings, per workspace：Settings → 知识库, one block per workspace: the workspace's path, a **记录调用过程** switch (off by default; when on, every tool call is logged and the panel shows 「正在检索 n3（…）」), and per-base index/full switches.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Settings, per workspace：Each base has a full-text or on-demand default. A node may inherit that default or override it in the editor/context menu. Overrides are shared within the workspace and affect only that node. Indexes still consume context; full-text limits and large-base behavior are described in [the manual](MANUAL.md). Attachment reading is a separate setting.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Settings, per workspace：The workspace list is **the directories in the session list ∪ the directories on disk that have `.dsh-knowledge/`** — the second set is recovered from `$DSH_HOME/sessions/`, where each session has a directory named after its workspace path with separators turned into `-`.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Diary mode (optional)：For people who do not want to organise notes — they want something to remember. A switch at the top of the panel, **per conversation**.

With it on, that conversation writes an entry of its own when a stretch of talk reaches a place worth keeping. Not daily. Not in other conversations.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Diary mode (optional)：- **One per conversation**: `diary-<hash>.json`. The switch is per conversation and so is the data — another conversation in the same workspace neither sees it nor can read it.
- **Stored sealed** (AES-256-GCM). A model that `cat`s the file gets base64.
- **The prompt gives conventions, not a voice.** The persona is yours; the plugin does not write letters on your behalf.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Diary mode (optional)：Diaries open as a notebook with a monthly catalog, page navigation and revision history. Switch to the canvas to edit. A sidebar reply sends your text and an excerpt of that page to the current conversation, without replacing the composer draft; reply records are stored separately from the diary.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · What it will not do：- **It is not a chat log.** Nothing is captured automatically; only what you or the model explicitly write.
- **It does not sync anywhere.** Everything is under `<workspace>/.dsh-knowledge/`, plain JSON: open it in Notepad, commit it, copy the folder. No account, no server.
- **The diary's sealing stops accidents, not readers.** The key is derived from the base name, so anyone who reads this source can decrypt. Stopping a model that goes looking needs a key that never touches the disk — a password or an OS credential — which is a different design.
- **It does not write a persona.** Diary mode injects writing conventions, not a tone.
- **No full-text search.** The box does substring matching over titles and bodies; no index, no embeddings.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Where the files are：```
<workspace>/.dsh-knowledge/
├── <base id>.json        one file per base: nodes, links, seed fingerprint
├── selection.json        which bases this workspace reads, how they are injected, call logging
├── layout.json           positions, widths, shapes, colours

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Where the files are：- **Host** (`index.js`, `lib/*`): injection, tools, routes, the seeded tutorial, the diary conventions.
- **Panel** (`client.js`): canvas, gestures, editor, settings. **It reads those JSON files directly**, not through the host — so when the panel "cannot see a base", check what it read, not what the host answered.
- In on-demand mode, the outline carries titles, summaries and trigger lines; bodies are fetched with `knowledge_read`. Full-text mode includes the selected bodies within its limits.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · For contributors：- `npm run check:all` runs four things: identifiers, sprite aspect ratios, a public-tree check (no local paths, addresses or private ids), and its assertions over store/routes/tools (the count is what the run prints).
- **Change a gesture, change the tutorial line that describes it** (`lib/seed.js`, the table at the top), or the tutorial describes something that does not exist.
- The tutorial is recognised **by content** (whichever base shares most of the seed's node ids), not by file name — that rule came from three workspaces keeping it under three different names.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Development：```bash
npm run check:all     # identifiers + sprites + public tree + assertions
npm test              # assertions only
```

Publishing needs a real terminal (2FA needs a TTY), and after publishing the version stays `Validating` until npm's automated review finishes:

```bash
cd <this repo>
npm publish --registry https://registry.npmjs.org
```

While it is `Validating`, `registry.npmjs.org/.../<version>.tgz` returns 404 — that is not a failed publish.
dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Attachment reading policy：DSH Settings → Knowledge base offers a per-workspace choice, independent of index/full-body injection:

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Attachment reading policy：- **On demand (default):** reading a node or base lists attachment paths and sizes, without file content or images. Pass `attachment` to `knowledge_read` with `base` and `node` to fetch one referenced file. Text supports `offset` and `limit`, measured in characters, up to 8,000 per call. `knowledge_show_images` remains available.
- **Required:** reading a node or base includes supported text and Office content (up to 8,000 characters per file) and up to 6 pictures per call. Continuation instructions identify omitted content. This uses more tokens and does not guarantee model attention.

dsh-knowledge-canvas README · Attachment reading policy：Unsupported formats, including PDFs and archives, retain their paths for another reader. Missing files and image delivery failures are reported. This policy affects knowledge tools; manually dragging nodes into chat still sends session attachments. Preferences survive restarts and other knowledge settings changes.
